title: How do you secure a CI/CD pipeline?
description: Use least-privilege tokens, signed commits, dependency scanning, and audit logs.

data.text: Question: How do you secure a CI/CD pipeline?
Use least-privilege service accounts, OIDC instead of long-lived secrets, dependency scanning, signed commits, and audit logging.

items: OIDC: federated credentials instead of secrets
Permissions: read-only by default, time-bound access
Scanning: Snyk or GitHub Dependabot for vulnerabilities
Signing: commit signing and image signatures
Audit: log pipeline events and alert on anomalies

data.code:
permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}
      - run: dotnet publish --configuration Release
